title: Origenes Adamantius: Tractatus super Leviticum
shelf_note: Rufinus' Latin of Origen's Homilies on Leviticus in a 12th/13th-c. textualis manuscript (HAB Wolfenbüttel); patristic exegesis, a reasonable neighbour to the library's theological sources. No tradition or collection set.
structure_note: 189 pages, 184 with OCR, 173 translated. The pages run in order (p.47 carries folio number 22). Each of the three pages read sits on the right leaf. Page 136 holds the homily break, and the OCR numbers it VI/VII where the red rubric reads xi/xii.

other.note: the invented marginal list is translated and shown as a margin note: 'And of the great priest, and of his office, and of his garments ... and of his death, and of his priesthood, and of his sons, and of his death.'

book_verdict: A real manuscript of Rufinus' Origen, read poorly by flash-lite. All three pages carry meaning-changing misreads that a fluent translation carries forward, two of them reversing the sense (p.47: 'not all is granted' → 'all things are granted'; p.136: 'that eternal fire not await us' → 'but rather the eternal fire'). Page 136 also has an invented, looping marginal list and the wrong homily numbers. Not showable as is; it needs a re-read on a stronger lane.

title: Disputatio theologica de baptismo et confirmatione. In alma academia Ingolstadiensi di martii M. D. XCV. Publicè proposita. Respondente M. Christophoro grentzing societatis Jesu, ss. Theologiae studioso.
shelf_note: A 1595 Jesuit theses print from Ingolstadt on baptism and confirmation; early modern Catholic theology. No tradition or collection set.
structure_note: 9 pages, 9 with OCR, 8 translated. The pages read are printed pp. 1, 3 and 4 (signatures A2, A3) and run in order; the catchwords match the next page. 'published: Unknown' although the title gives March 1595: a catalogue gap.

tr_errors.english: of which none, except the first, can be omitted while saving the Sacrament entirely
tr_errors.problem: 'penitus' misplaced; the sense is 'none except the first can be omitted at all with the sacrament intact'

ocr_errors.image: no signature printed at the foot of p.4 (only show-through of 'A 3')

title: Icones Fungorum Niskiensium
shelf_note: Schweinitz's manuscript watercolour plates of fungi from Niesky (c.1805), Farlow Library, Harvard; early modern natural history, in the botany/biodiversity collections it carries.
structure_note: 110 pages, all with OCR, 67 translated. The book is mostly plates with captions, so 'translation' means translating species labels. Page 3 is the pastedown/flyleaf with a modern Farlow bookplate (a provenance mark, not a rights issue). It is tagged title-page.

ocr_errors.image: a pastedown/flyleaf with a pencilled label and a bookplate
ocr_errors.problem: page type wrong

other.note: broken markup in the translation: '<margin></margin> <note>…</note> </margin>' three times, so stray closing tags reach the reader
the stored summary says the fungi were 'found in the Nisko region'; Niskiensium is Niesky (Saxony), not Nisko

tr_errors.problem: invented common name (Agaricus/Crepidotus variabilis is not an oyster mushroom); every label gets an invented vernacular gloss

book_verdict: The captions are transcribed accurately and the plates come through intact. The flaws are cosmetic but visible: stray closing tags on the flyleaf, invented vernacular glosses on the species names, and a summary that places Niesky in 'Nisko'. Showable after a markup fix.

title: Epistolae familiares, Historica Bohemica
shelf_note: A humanist manuscript (Harvard) of Pius II's letters and Historia Bohemica; Renaissance Latin source, fits a primary-source library. No tradition or collection set.
structure_note: 665 pages, 664 with OCR, 660 translated. The pages read are on their right leaves (folio 81, letter XXXVII, Historia Bohemica). Nothing structural stands out.

ocr_errors.problem: 'dangerous to the commonwealth' read as 'the rapine dangerous'
Federico's title 'captain of our troops' becomes a garble, then glossed 'an abundance of mercy'
concessive 'although' read as 'quoque', which flips the sentence (see tr_errors)

tr_errors.source: Neque arbitreris quoque Rex Francie noster amicus indutias in Regno Sicilie quaerat ... Nos unquam passuros
tr_errors.english: Nor should you think that the King of France, our friend, seeks a truce in the Kingdom of Sicily, or wishes to include Sigismund as a friend. We will never allow ...
tr_errors.problem: the source says: do not think, ALTHOUGH the King of France seeks a truce and wants to include Sigismund, that we will ever allow ... The English denies what the Pope affirms about the French king
a gloss invented over a misread

other.note: the translation opens with '<meta>continues from previous page</meta>' although the page begins a new letter under an illuminated initial

ocr_errors.problem: the cardinal's name (Domenico [Capranica]) read as 'domino', so the name is lost

tr_errors.source: nobilitas ... periculorum belli contemptrix ac promissi tenax
tr_errors.english: contemptuous of what is promised, and tenacious of their own
tr_errors.problem: 'keeping its promises' turned into 'contemptuous of what is promised', which reverses the praise

book_verdict: A good transcription overall of a clean humanist hand, with faithful translation on most lines. On p.331 a misread concessive makes the Pope deny that the French king seeks a truce, and p.497 reverses the praise of the Bohemian nobility. Showable with caveats.

title: Ad praetantissimum patrem et meritissimum Rhavenatem antistitem Philiam Roverellam Angeli Callimachi Siculi, in libellum de oratione
shelf_note: Angelus Callimachus's 1492 humanist dialogue on prayer and the Lord's Prayer, in a microfilm of a manuscript; devotional theology. No tradition or collection set.
structure_note: 32 pages, 32 with OCR, 31 translated. Each page record is an unsplit two-page opening (folios numbered 7, 13, 21 at the gutter foot); the OCR handles it as two columns. On p.25 the translation drops the left-hand page entirely.
